title: Kellen Moore on injury report, Falcons pass rush | Saints vs. Falcons 2026 NFL Week 4
headline: Saints enter Monday night at Atlanta with Kaden Elliss, Carl Granderson and Anfernee Jennings out; Pete Werner and Noah Fant are questionable, and Fant's status will be decided close to kickoff.
summary: Kellen Moore's injury report had three players out: Kaden Elliss (calf), Carl Granderson (ankle) and Anfernee Jennings (knee). Pete Werner (shoulder) and Noah Fant (abdominal) are questionable, and everyone else has no designation. Elliss's calf injury was described only as week to week. Moore said Fant did not practice this week and may be evaluated through the weekend, with a possible pregame workout. The evaluation will focus on contact strength and how he feels after a stinger-type injury. Nathan Shepherd had a planned rest day. With the linebackers thinned, Moore praised Danny Stutsman and said he could start for plenty of teams. On the roster side, Devin Neal and Audric Estime were released with injury settlements, which Moore called a roster-management decision about preserving injured-reserve return slots. Moore said a player named Jordan is ramping up in meetings and rehab with no return timeline, and that the venues have no bearing on it. He called the Falcons rivalry authentic and noted they were 0-2 against Atlanta last year. He praised Atlanta's pass rush, which creates one-on-ones even without their top two edge rushers, and said Michael Penix Jr. played well in Green Bay.

topics.detail: Devin Neal and Audric Estime were released with injury settlements instead of staying on IR. Moore said the team has limited IR-return slots and wants to save some for later in the season.
With Elliss and Jennings out, Moore said run defense depends on the next man up, and the replacements have had full weeks of practice reps.
Moore credited the defense's good tackling to constant fundamentals work and takeaway drills. He said the offense needs to improve at ball security.
A player named Jordan is rehabbing with trainers and getting meeting-room work. There is no return timeline, and the overseas and New York games don't factor in.
Moore called the Falcons a confident team coming off a good game at Green Bay. He praised Penix and their pass rush, which creates one-on-ones even without their top two edge rushers.
